Overview

Hangzhou as a Business Centre

Hangzhou is the capital of Zhejiang province and one of China's leading centres for the digital economy. The city's GDP passed 2.3 trillion yuan in 2025, growing 5.2 percent, according to the municipal government's work report, with goods exports above 600 billion yuan. Core digital economy industries added about 630.5 billion yuan of value in 2024, about 28.8 percent of city GDP, and the city aims to raise that share above 30 percent. Hangzhou became China's first cross-border e-commerce comprehensive pilot zone in 2015 and now hosts more than 65,000 sellers trading internationally. It also includes the Hangzhou Area of the China (Zhejiang) Pilot Free Trade Zone and a growing artificial intelligence sector.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Hangzhou mainly because of its weight in online commerce and its dense base of private manufacturers and traders. Brand owners need to identify the businesses behind infringing listings and counterfeit goods sold through platforms and cross-border channels. Importers and retailers need to verify suppliers and sellers before onboarding them, and to understand related-party and trading company structures that can conceal the real manufacturer. Investors in Hangzhou technology and artificial intelligence companies want background research on founders and shareholders. Disputes over online contracts, copyright and domain names may come before the Hangzhou Internet Court, so counsel often needs facts about online operators established in a form Chinese courts accept.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Hangzhou

01

Online infringement and counterfeiting research

Identification of the operators, companies and supply chains behind infringing listings and counterfeit goods associated with Hangzhou sellers, using business registration records, platform storefront information, test purchases arranged through counsel and open sources, to support platform takedowns, administrative complaints and litigation.

02

Cross-border e-commerce seller verification

Background checks on Hangzhou-based sellers, logistics providers and brand partners before onboarding or contract, testing registration details, ownership, related companies, litigation and administrative penalties, and whether the stated business matches its online footprint and export activity.

03

Supplier and manufacturer due diligence

Verification that a Zhejiang supplier is the manufacturer it claims to be rather than a trading intermediary, with review of registered capital, shareholders, affiliated companies, court judgments and enforcement listings, supporting procurement, quality and anti-forced labour supply chain programmes.

04

Technology and AI investment checks

Research on founders, shareholders and senior managers of Hangzhou technology and artificial intelligence companies, including prior ventures, disputes, judgment-debtor listings and media coverage, scoped to avoid areas where Chinese data, state secrets and counter-espionage rules restrict information gathering.

05

Digital evidence for court proceedings

Support to Chinese counsel in preparing facts about online operators for disputes before the Hangzhou Internet Court or other courts, coordinating notarised or electronically preserved evidence through properly qualified providers, so that material can be assessed under Chinese evidence rules.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Hangzhou

Hangzhou Internet Court

Opened on 18 August 2017 on the basis of the Hangzhou Railway Transport Court, the Hangzhou Internet Court was China's first court dedicated to internet-related disputes. It hears cases such as online shopping and online service contract disputes and online copyright and intellectual property claims, runs proceedings largely online, and was the first Chinese court to accept blockchain records as evidence of web content. Similar courts later opened in Beijing and Guangzhou.

Courts and arbitration

Other commercial disputes in the city are heard by the basic people's courts and the Hangzhou Intermediate People's Court, with the Zhejiang Higher People's Court also located in Hangzhou. Domestic arbitration is administered by the Hangzhou Arbitration Commission, while international parties often choose national or offshore institutions. Published judgments and enforcement information are useful sources, but coverage is incomplete and must be checked carefully.

Cross-border e-commerce pilot zone

Hangzhou became China's first cross-border e-commerce comprehensive pilot zone in 2015. Local media report annual cross-border e-commerce trade above 152 billion yuan and more than 65,000 sellers operating internationally, and the city hosts the Global Cross-Border E-Commerce Trade Expo. The concentration of sellers, service providers and logistics firms makes Hangzhou a frequent point of origin in brand protection and marketplace fraud inquiries.

Free trade zone and investment

The Hangzhou Area of the China (Zhejiang) Pilot Free Trade Zone focuses on digital trade and related services. Foreign-invested enterprises in the city register with local market regulation authorities, and their basic registration and administrative penalty information is available through China's national enterprise credit information system. Deeper filings and shareholder documents are usually obtained through counsel and may be restricted.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Hangzhou

For matters touching Hangzhou, TDSC begins with a jurisdictional and legal-risk review with the client's PRC counsel, because Chinese personal information, data export, state secrets and counter-espionage rules limit what can be collected and taken out of the country. Research relies on lawful public sources: enterprise credit and registration records, published judgments and enforcement listings, platform storefront information, trade data and media. Any test purchases, site visits or evidence preservation are carried out by properly qualified professionals in China under counsel's direction, often with notarisation. TDSC does not use pretexting, buy personal data or access restricted systems, and minimises personal information in reports. TDSC has no office in Hangzhou or elsewhere in China.

TDSC has no office in Hangzhou. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Hangzhou: Frequently Asked Questions

Can TDSC identify who is behind an infringing online store linked to Hangzhou?

Often, within limits. TDSC links storefront details, business registration records, trademarks, related companies and open-source information to identify the likely operator and connected entities. Formal disclosure from platforms or courts, test purchases and notarised evidence are handled through Chinese counsel and qualified providers. Results are presented with confidence levels, not as certainties.

What is special about the Hangzhou Internet Court?

It was China's first court dedicated to internet disputes, opened in 2017. It hears online shopping and service contract disputes and online copyright and related claims, largely through online proceedings, and accepted blockchain records as evidence early. TDSC helps counsel assemble facts about online operators; counsel decides how evidence is preserved and presented.

Can TDSC confirm that a Hangzhou supplier is a real manufacturer?

TDSC can test the claim using registration records, business scope, shareholders, affiliates, judgments, administrative penalties and online footprint, which often reveals whether a company is a trading intermediary. Where a site visit is needed, it is arranged through qualified professionals in China and scoped with counsel to comply with Chinese law.

Are there limits on due diligence in Hangzhou?

Yes. Chinese law restricts collection and export of personal information and important data, and state secrets and counter-espionage rules can apply to information about state-linked or sensitive sectors. TDSC scopes each matter with PRC counsel, uses only lawful public sources and qualified local professionals, and declines work that would require restricted methods.

Does TDSC have an office or investigators in Hangzhou?

No. TDSC has no office, staff or address in Hangzhou or anywhere in China. Engagements are run from Nashville. Where local inquiries are lawful and necessary, TDSC coordinates properly qualified professionals in China and works with the client's PRC counsel within an agreed written scope.
